Write a descriptive, fictional, imaginative screenplay of a 127 year old man receiving the world record for oldest human to ever live. Later that night, in bed, he recalls a theory he read on the internet in his youth, \"Quantum Immortality\" he then proceeds to have a mental breakdown.\n Write the entire response in title case (capitalize the first letter of every major word).assistant
response:
FADE IN:

INT. RECORDS OFFICE - DAY

The room is filled with officials, reporters, and cameras. A large banner reads "WORLD RECORD HOLDER" in bold letters. At the center of the room, a frail but determined 127-year-old man, GEORGE, is seated in a wheelchair. He is surrounded by his family and friends, all beaming with pride.

GEORGE
(whispering to himself)
I Did It. I Really Did It.

The officials present George with a certificate and a gold medal, proclaiming him the oldest human to ever live.

REPORTER 1
(congratulating George)
Mr. George, this is an incredible achievement. You are an inspiration to us all.

GEORGE
(smiling weakly)
Thank You. I'm Just Glad To Be Here.

The ceremony ends, and George is wheeled out of the room, surrounded by his loved ones.

CUT TO:

INT. GEORGE'S BEDROOM - NIGHT

George lies in bed, his eyes fixed on the ceiling. He looks old and tired, but his mind is still sharp. He begins to think back to his youth, when he spent countless hours browsing the internet.

GEORGE
(to himself)
Quantum Immortality... I Remember Reading About That Theory...

Suddenly, George's expression changes. His eyes widen, and his face contorts in a mixture of fear and confusion.

GEORGE
(whispering)
What If It's True? What If I'm Not Really Dead?

George's mind starts to unravel. He begins to see visions of himself living multiple lives, experiencing different realities. He sees himself as a young man, full of life and energy, and then as an old man, frail and weak.

GEORGE
(panicked)
No, No, No! This Can't Be Happening!

George's body starts to shake, and he begins to sob uncontrollably. He throws off the covers and gets out of bed, pacing back and forth in his room.

GEORGE
(whispering)
I'm Not Alone. I'm Not Alone...

Suddenly, George's eyes lock onto a small, dusty book on his nightstand. It's an old copy of "The Many-Worlds Interpretation of Quantum Mechanics".

GEORGE
(whispering)
It's True. It's All True.

George's mind is consumed by the theory. He starts to see the world in a different light, as a multiverse of infinite possibilities.

GEORGE
(whispering)
I'm Not Dead. I'm Just... Different.

George's body collapses to the floor, and he lies there, staring at the ceiling, lost in a world of his own making.

FADE TO BLACK.

FADE IN:

INT. GEORGE'S BEDROOM - LATER

George lies on the floor, his eyes closed. His body is still, but his mind is racing. He's trapped in a world of quantum uncertainty, where the laws of reality no longer apply.

GEORGE
(whispering)
I'm Not Alone. I'm Not Alone...

The camera zooms out, and the room fades to black, leaving the audience wondering: what is real, and what is just a product of George's fractured mind?
